result.question: Does processor power stay constant across idle, normal, heavy, and burst workloads? Describe the stated pattern.
result.answer:
No, processor power does not stay constant. 

The stated pattern is:
- When the CPU is idle, it consumes low power.
- When running normal programs, it consumes moderate power.
- When performing heavy calculations, it consumes high power.
- During short bursts of activity, it may demand very high peak power.

retrieved_chunks.text: MAXIMUM POWER A PROCESSOR EVER REQUIRES? A processor does not consume a constant amount of power. For example: When the CPU is idle → low power When running normal programs → moderate power When performing heavy calculations → high power During short bursts of activity → it may demand very high peak power

ENERGY EFFICIENCY STRATEGIES • Modern microprocessors offer many techniques to try to improve energy efficiency despite flat clock rates and constant supply voltages: • 1. Do nothing well. Most microprocessors today turn off the clock of inactive modules to save energy and dynamic power. For example, if no floating-point instructions are executing, the clock of the floating-point unit is disabled. If some cores are idle, their clocks are stopped.

ENERGY EFFICIENCY STRATEGIES • Design for the typical case. • PMDs and laptops are often idle • Use low power mode DRAM to save energy • Spin disk at lower rate • PCs use emergency slowdown if program execution causes overheating

ENERGY AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY The key idea is that power and energy are not the same thing, and when comparing processors for a particular task, energy is usually the better metric.
